tasks.title: Give a notification an optional action control: rendered beside the message, removed with focus moved like the dismiss control on activation, and carried through keyed replacement
acceptance: C1. `src/renderer/src/notifications/types.ts` declares `NotificationAction` as `{ label: string; onAction: () => void }` and adds `action?: NotificationAction` to `NotificationRequest`, exactly as `contracts/notification-action.ts` declares them. `index.ts` re-exports `NotificationAction` as a type. No runtime export is added: the existing test 'ships exactly the contract’s runtime exports, with the contract’s test ids' (`NotificationProvider.test.tsx:113-126` at e2e3b0a) passes with its assertions unchanged, and `NOTIFICATION_TEST_IDS` is unchanged. The type-pin test at `:128-150` is updated so its `NotificationRequest` pin (`:130-134`) includes `action?: NotificationAction`, and it gains `expectTypeOf<NotificationAction>().toEqualTypeOf<{ label: string; onAction: () => void }>()`. These pins are compile-time only; the repo-wide `npm run typecheck` that checks them is T3's C61, and this task's report says so rather than running it.

C2 (preserved, newly tested; passes at e2e3b0a by design). A new test shows that, for each of `error`, `info` and `success`, an item raised WITHOUT `action` has exactly three element children in this order: the `aria-hidden` marker `span`, the message element (`role` `alert` or `status`), and the dismiss `button`. The item holds exactly one `button`, and the message element has no `id` attribute. What it preserves: a notification raised without an action renders exactly as it does today (`NotificationItem.tsx:46-67` at e2e3b0a).

C3. A new test shows that an item raised WITH `action: { label, onAction }` has exactly four element children in this order: marker, message element, action control, dismiss control. The action control is an `HTMLButtonElement` with `type="button"`, it is not inside the message element, its `textContent` equals `label`, `within(item).getByRole('button', { name: label })` returns it, and it carries no `aria-label` and no `aria-labelledby` attribute. The message element's `textContent` is still exactly `message`, and for a non-empty message its `childNodes.length` is 1. The native button encodes the binding frontend rules under 'Accessibility floor': 'Every interactive element is reachable and operable by keyboard alone' and 'Semantic elements are used for their meaning'. Red step: write the test first, run `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/notifications/NotificationProvider.test.tsx` before the implementation exists, and report the failure.

C4. A new test raises two items that carry actions with the SAME label and different messages. For each item, the action control's `aria-describedby` is a non-empty id, and `document.getElementById(<that id>)` is that same item's message element, not the other item's. Red step as in C3.

C5. A new test activates an item's action control with `fireEvent.click`. The `onAction` passed for it (a `vi.fn()`) has been called exactly once. Afterwards that item is gone from the viewport, and every other live item is still there with its message unchanged. Red step as in C3.

C6. A new test with three items activates the action control of the MIDDLE item. Afterwards `document.activeElement` is the dismiss control (`Dismiss notification`) of the item that followed it. This encodes the binding frontend rule under 'Accessibility floor': 'Focus is visible, and it moves predictably after an action that changes what is on screen', with the target the provider already uses for its dismiss control (`handleDismissControl`, `NotificationProvider.tsx:201-207` at e2e3b0a).

C7. A new test with two items activates the action control of the LAST one. Afterwards `document.activeElement` is the dismiss control of the item that preceded it. This encodes the same 'Accessibility floor' rule as C6.

C8. A new test with one item activates its action control. Afterwards `document.activeElement` is the viewport element (`data-testid="notification-viewport"`). This encodes the same 'Accessibility floor' rule as C6.

C9. A new test raises a keyed item, `key: 'k'`, whose `onAction` synchronously calls `notify` with the same key, a different message and an action. After the action control is activated, the viewport holds exactly one item. Its message is the new message, it has an action control, and `document.activeElement` is the viewport element, because there was no neighbour when the control was activated.

C10. A new test raises a keyed item with action A (label `'First'`), then calls `notify` with the same key and action B (label `'Second'`). The viewport holds exactly one item. Its action control's `textContent` is `Second`. Activating it calls B's callback once and A's zero times. At e2e3b0a a keyed replacement copies only `kind` and `message` (`addOrReplace`, `NotificationProvider.tsx:96-101`).

C11. A new test raises a keyed item with an action, then calls `notify` with the same key and NO `action`. The viewport holds exactly one item, it has exactly one `button` (the dismiss control), and its message is the second message.

C12. A new test raises a keyed item without an action, then calls `notify` with the same key and an action. The viewport holds exactly one item, and it now has the action control, labelled with the second request's label.

C13 (preserved, newly tested). A new test raises an `info` item with an action. It is removed at exactly `autoDismissMs`, the same timing the existing 'removes info at exactly autoDismissMs (C3)' test asserts for an item without an action. (That `(C3)` is an earlier session's label, not this manifest's.)
C14 (preserved, newly tested). A new test raises an `error` item with an action. It is still present after ten times `autoDismissMs`.

C15. Discrimination, keyed replacement: once the implementation is in place, inject a defect at the ONE site where `addOrReplace`'s replacement branch takes the new request's action, so that the replacement keeps the existing item's action instead. Run `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/notifications/NotificationProvider.test.tsx`, observe C10 and C11 fail, revert, and confirm the revert by reading the line back before running anything wider. The report names the file:line, the text injected, the failing test names and the revert. The injection must type-check at its site.

C16. Discrimination, focus: inject a defect into the action control's activation handler only (not into `handleDismissControl`), so that it records no focus target before removing the item. Run the same scoped command, observe at least C6 and C8 fail while the existing dismiss-control focus tests ('moves focus to the remaining item’s dismiss control after the first is dismissed (C18)' and the two beside it) still pass, revert, and confirm. The report names the site, the command, the output and the revert.

C17. The stylesheet gives the action control a rule that uses only `--oc-*` tokens, and a `:focus-visible` rule for it that declares `outline: var(--oc-border-thick) solid var(--oc-focus-ring)`, the declaration `.dismiss:focus-visible` has (`Notifications.module.css:71-73` at e2e3b0a). `Notifications.styles.test.ts` asserts that outline for the new selector through its own `ruleFor`, for example by adding the selector to the 'focus rings' list at `:85`. Red step: write that assertion first, run `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/notifications/Notifications.styles.test.ts` against the unmodified stylesheet, and report the failure. Only then edit the CSS.

C18 (preserved). In `Notifications.styles.test.ts`, the token test ('references only tokens that the frozen TOKENS map names (C21)'), the hardcoded-colour test, 'never fights the cascade and never removes the focus ring' and the focus-ring assertions for `.viewport:focus-visible` and `.dismiss:focus-visible` all pass, and each keeps every assertion it has at e2e3b0a. `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/__tests__/hygiene.test.ts` exits 0. That file scans the whole renderer tree as text for colour, px font sizes, font weights, letter-spacing and border-width tokens, so it covers the new rule too. It also reads T2's files, which T2 changes only in ways those rules do not inspect.

C19. The docblocks state the new rules in place. In `types.ts`, the docblocks of `NotificationAction` and `action` say: the label is the control's whole accessible name; `onAction` is called once per activation, after the item's removal is requested; a keyed replacement replaces the action, or removes it when the new request has none; and without `action` the item is unchanged. `NotificationItem.tsx`'s leading docblock names the action control as a sibling of the message element, between it and the dismiss control. The FOCUS paragraph of `NotificationProvider.tsx` (`:15-17` at e2e3b0a) says the action control moves focus to the same target the dismiss control does, and still says that `notify` and `dismiss` never move focus.

C20. `types.ts`'s header (`:1-7` at e2e3b0a) no longer cites the frozen contract's path under `.sir/sessions` (`:3`). Once the action is added, its claim that the file holds the declarations of that contract is no longer true. The header says in place that this file is the single declaration site and `index.ts` the only import surface. Check: `git grep -c --untracked .sir/sessions -- src/renderer/src/notifications` prints `src/renderer/src/notifications/types.ts:1` at e2e3b0a, and at T1's tip prints nothing and exits 1. `git grep -c --untracked -E "20261[01][0-9]{2}-[0-9]{4}" -- src/renderer/src/notifications` prints `src/renderer/src/notifications/types.ts:1` at e2e3b0a, and at T1's tip prints nothing and exits 1.

C21. No existing test is weakened. In `git diff -U0 -- src/renderer/src/notifications/NotificationProvider.test.tsx src/renderer/src/notifications/Notifications.styles.test.ts`, the only removed lines (lines beginning with a single `-`) are inside the `NotificationRequest` type pin (`NotificationProvider.test.tsx:130-134` at e2e3b0a) and the 'focus rings' selector list (`Notifications.styles.test.ts:85`), and no `it(` title present at e2e3b0a is removed or renamed.

C22. Every new test's name states its condition and its expected outcome, says neither 'works' nor 'is correct', and claims no more than it asserts. This encodes the binding test discipline rules under `Naming`.

C23. `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/notifications` exits 0 with every injection reverted. The report quotes vitest's `Test Files` and `Tests` summary lines. This task runs no repo-wide command (`npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build`): T2 is editing the same worktree concurrently, and T3 runs those commands.

tasks.title: Add retryLanes and retryRoutingMode to WorkspaceActions, clear routingModeError on a retry, and reword the no-retry and backfill docblocks
acceptance: C24. `WorkspaceActions` in `src/renderer/src/contracts/renderer-state.ts` (`:521` at e2e3b0a) declares `retryLanes(podId: PodId): Promise<ActionResult<void>>` and `retryRoutingMode(): Promise<ActionResult<void>>`, exactly as `contracts/workspace-retry-actions.ts` declares them. Each has a docblock that states that contract's rules in place: for `retryLanes`, the synchronous `'loading'`/`null` write, the same-object failure, the coalescing and the absence of activation; for `retryRoutingMode`, the no-op once the mode is resolved, the coalescing, `routingModeError` being `null` while in flight, and the same-object failure. `WorkspaceStateStore` implements both. `git grep -c -E "retryLanes|retryRoutingMode" -- src` prints nothing and exits 1 at e2e3b0a.

C25. A new test in `store.test.ts` starts with `laneList` failed through `failInvoke`, activates the Pod with `setActivePod`, and waits for `lanesPhase` `'error'`. It then calls `clearInvokeFailure('laneList')` and `await store.actions.retryLanes(POD)`. The result is `{ ok: true }`, `lanesPhase` is `'ready'`, `lanesError` is `null`, `lanes` equals the stub's answer, and `api.calls.laneList` has length 2. Red step: write it first, run `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/state/store.test.ts` before `retryLanes` exists, and report the failure.

C26. A new test calls `retryLanes` while `lanes.list` keeps failing with a second `IpcError` object, distinct from the first. The result's `error` and the runtime's `lanesError` are each `toBe` that second object, and `lanesPhase` is `'error'`.

C27. A new test holds `lanes.list` on a deferred promise and calls `retryLanes` without awaiting it. Before the promise settles, `lanesPhase` is `'loading'` and `lanesError` is `null`. This encodes the binding frontend rule under 'Data fetching': 'Every fetch has a declared loading state, a declared error state, and a declared empty state'.

C28. A new test holds the lane load that `setActivePod` starts on a deferred promise, calls `retryLanes` for the same Pod twice before it settles, and then settles it. Exactly one `lanes.list` call was made in total, and both retry results equal that load's outcome. This encodes the header rule of `WorkspaceActions` (`renderer-state.ts:516-520` at e2e3b0a): 'the state layer, not the component, is responsible for suppressing a redundant in-flight duplicate'.

C29. A new test starts the store with `appRoutingMode` failed, so `routingModeError` is non-null and `routingMode` is `null`. It then calls `clearInvokeFailure('appRoutingMode')` and `await store.actions.retryRoutingMode()`. The result is `{ ok: true }`, `routingMode` is `'lanes'`, `routingModeError` is `null`, and `api.calls.appRoutingMode` has length 2. At e2e3b0a a successful routing-mode read never clears `routingModeError`: the only write of that field in `store.ts` is the failure branch at `:322`. Red step as in C25.

C30. A new test calls `retryRoutingMode` after a failed startup read while the channel keeps failing with a second, distinct `IpcError`. `routingModeError` is `toBe` that second object, the result's `error` is the same object, and `routingMode` is `null`.

C31. A new test holds `app.routingMode` on a deferred promise for the retry, and calls `retryRoutingMode` without awaiting it after a failed startup read. Before the promise settles, `routingModeError` is `null`. This encodes the same 'Data fetching' rule as C27.

C32. A new test calls `retryRoutingMode` after a SUCCESSFUL startup read. The result is `{ ok: true }`, `api.calls.appRoutingMode` still has length 1, `routingMode` is unchanged and `routingModeError` stays `null`.
C33. A new test calls `start()` and then `retryRoutingMode()` before the startup read settles. `api.calls.appRoutingMode` has length 1 once both have settled, and both outcomes agree.

C34. `ACTION_CASES` in `store.test.ts` (`:133` at e2e3b0a) gains a `laneList` case run through `retryLanes` and an `appRoutingMode` case run through `retryRoutingMode`, so the existing per-case tests ('<channel>: passes the IpcError through unmodified' and '<channel>: a rejecting preload becomes INTERNAL, not an unhandled rejection') run for both channels and pass. Every other member of that table already has those two tests, so the new members get them too. The table's docblock no longer says that `laneList` and `appRoutingMode` 'have no action of their own' (`:118-120` at e2e3b0a): `git grep -c "have no action of their own" -- src/renderer/src/state/store.test.ts` prints `src/renderer/src/state/store.test.ts:1` at e2e3b0a, and at T2's tip prints nothing and exits 1.

C35. Both enumeration tests list the two new members and pass. `ACTION_NAMES` in `workspace-provider.test.tsx` (`:101-122` at e2e3b0a) includes `'retryLanes'` and `'retryRoutingMode'`, and 'exposes every WorkspaceActions method and nothing else' passes. The per-action `args` table in `store.test.ts` (`:1154-1175` at e2e3b0a) gives arguments for both, and its test passes with its 'a method added without a case here fails' check intact.

C36 (preserved, newly tested). E9's retry is `loadMoreEvents`, unchanged. A new test fails `eventsRead`, calls `loadMoreEvents(POD)`, clears the failure, and calls it again. `api.calls.eventsRead` has length 2, and the second call's argument deep-equals the first, so the same page (same `afterSeq`) is read again. What it preserves: the no-op is keyed on `phase === 'ready' && !hasMore` only (`store.ts:853` at e2e3b0a), and a failed read leaves `cursorSeq` unchanged.

C37. The docblocks state retry where they used to deny it. In `renderer-state.ts`: the `routingMode` docblock (`:142-151` at e2e3b0a, 'Resolved once at startup') says the mode is resolved by the startup read or, after that fails, by `retryRoutingMode`, and is constant once resolved; the `routingModeError` docblock (`:153-166`) states the reworded rule of `contracts/workspace-retry-actions.ts`; and the `loadMoreEvents` docblock (`:682-686`) no longer says it is a no-op when `backfill.hasMore` is false, but says the no-op needs phase `'ready'` and that a call after a failed read re-reads the same page. In `store.ts`, the `loadRoutingMode` docblock (`:311-315`) names `retryRoutingMode` as the second writer. Check: `git grep -c -i "no retry" -- src/renderer/src/contracts/renderer-state.ts src/renderer/src/state/store.ts` prints `renderer-state.ts:1` and `store.ts:1` (full paths) at e2e3b0a, and at T2's tip prints nothing and exits 1.

C38. The `routingModeError` docblock's citation 'Amendment frozen in session 20261111-0156-message-alerting (`contracts/workspace-store-routing-error.ts`)' (`renderer-state.ts:164-165` at e2e3b0a) is removed: the rule it points at says 'No retry', which this task makes false. No new citation is added. Check: `git grep -c --untracked -E "20261[01][0-9]{2}-[0-9]{4}" -- src/renderer/src/contracts/renderer-state.ts src/renderer/src/state` prints `src/renderer/src/contracts/renderer-state.ts:1` at e2e3b0a, and at T2's tip prints nothing and exits 1. `git grep -c --untracked .sir/sessions -- src/renderer/src/contracts/renderer-state.ts src/renderer/src/state` prints nothing and exits 1, both at e2e3b0a and at T2's tip.

C39. Discrimination, coalescing: inject a defect into `store.ts` so that a lane load for a Pod is no longer registered as in flight and each call issues its own `lanes.list`. Run `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/state/store.test.ts`, observe C28 fail, revert, and confirm the revert by reading the line back. The report names the file:line, the text injected and the output. The injection must type-check at its site.

C40. Discrimination, the in-flight null: inject a defect into `store.ts` that removes `retryRoutingMode`'s write of `routingModeError: null` before the call. Run the same scoped command, observe C31 fail, revert and confirm. The report also says whether C29 failed under the same injection. That shows whether the success path clears the error on its own; either answer is acceptable, but it must be reported.

C41. Discrimination, same object: inject a defect at the ONE site where a failed lane load writes `lanesError` (`store.ts:992` at e2e3b0a, `lanesError: result.error,`, which occurs once in the file at e2e3b0a), making it a copy: `lanesError: { ...result.error },`. Run the same scoped command, observe C26 fail, revert and confirm. If the implementation moved that write, the report names the new file:line.

C42. No existing test is weakened. `git diff -U0 -- src/renderer/src/state/store.test.ts src/renderer/src/state/workspace-provider.test.tsx` removes no `it(` or `describe(` line present at e2e3b0a, and no `expect(` line except where a replaced line carries the same assertion. The existing test 'surfaces a failed page in the backfill Loadable and allows a retry' (`store.test.ts:717-731` at e2e3b0a) and the three `appRoutingMode` tests at `:396-433` keep every assertion they have.

tasks.title: Give E8, E9 and E10 a Retry action that re-runs the failed load, dismiss E10 once routingModeError clears, and run the repo-wide gates
acceptance: C45. In `src/renderer/src/shell/WorkspaceAlerts.test.tsx`, a new test mounts the app with `mountWorkspace` and `lanes.list` failing, and waits for the E8 item. That item holds exactly one button whose accessible name is `Retry`, besides `Dismiss notification`. The test then makes `lanes.list` answer `{ ok: true }` with at least one lane, and clicks `Retry`. Exactly two `lanes.list` calls were made in total, counted through `api.calls.laneList` or through a counter in a test-local override. No E8 item remains, and the lane rail (`TEST_IDS.laneRail`) shows a `TEST_IDS.laneRow` for each lane in that answer. Note that the stub's channel overrides beat `failInvoke` (`failure-paths.e2e.test.tsx:202-203` at e2e3b0a), so a test that needs a fail-then-succeed answer arranges it in one override. Red step: write the test first, run `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/shell/WorkspaceAlerts.test.tsx` against `WorkspaceAlerts.tsx` as at e2e3b0a (it passes no action), and report the failure.

C46. A new test clicks E8's `Retry` while `lanes.list` keeps failing. Two `lanes.list` calls were made, and the viewport then holds exactly one E8 error item reading the failure's message, which again carries a `Retry` button.

C47. A new test mounts with lanes answering and `events.read` failing, and waits for the E9 item. It then clears the failure and clicks that item's `Retry`. `api.calls.eventsRead` has length 2, the second call's argument deep-equals the first, and no E9 item remains.
C48. A new test clicks E9's `Retry` while `events.read` keeps failing. Two `events.read` calls were made, and the viewport then holds exactly one E9 error item, which carries a `Retry` button.

C49. A new test mounts with `app.routingMode` failing and waits for the E10 item. At that point `TEST_IDS.laneRail` is absent, because the shell shows the loading workspace while the mode is `null` (`App.tsx:146-152` at e2e3b0a). The test then clears the failure and clicks `Retry`. `api.calls.appRoutingMode` has length 2, no E10 item remains, and `TEST_IDS.laneRail` is present.

C50. A new test clicks E10's `Retry` while `app.routingMode` keeps failing with the same `IpcError` object the stub hands back on every call (`stub-api.ts:564-565` at e2e3b0a). Two `app.routingMode` calls were made, and the viewport then holds exactly one E10 error item, which carries a `Retry` button. This item is re-raised only because `routingModeError` passes through `null` while the retry is in flight (`contracts/workspace-retry-actions.ts`).

C51. E10 is dismissed by key whenever `routingModeError` is `null`. The E10 effect (`WorkspaceAlerts.tsx:71-74` at e2e3b0a) calls `notifier.dismiss('routing-mode')` in its `null` branch, where today it returns. This implements the Gate 1 decision in `discussion.md` under 'Decisions': 'E10 newly, once `routingModeError` clears'. A new test raises E10 and then drives `retryRoutingMode` NOT through the Retry button but through `useWorkspaceActions()`, from a component rendered inside the same providers as a real `WorkspaceAlerts` and `NotificationProvider`. It lets the retry succeed and finds the E10 item gone. Without the `dismiss` branch nothing removes it, because the button never ran. Discrimination: with the implementation in place, inject a defect that restores the early `return` in that `null` branch, run `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/shell/WorkspaceAlerts.test.tsx`, observe this test fail, revert, and confirm the revert by reading the line back. The report names the file:line.

C52. Activating Retry removes the item at once (decided at Gate 2). A new test holds `lanes.list` on a deferred promise for the retry and clicks E8's `Retry`. Before the promise settles, the viewport holds no E8 item.

C53 (preserved). The existing tests in `WorkspaceAlerts.test.tsx` pass with every assertion they have at e2e3b0a, including 'raises one error item, not two, for a single lanes-load failure under StrictMode' and 'removes the E8 error item once the same Pod’s lane load succeeds'. `git diff -U0 -- src/renderer/src/shell/WorkspaceAlerts.test.tsx` removes no `it(` or `expect(` line present at e2e3b0a.

C54. Each Retry action is built from the contract's action shape, `{ label: 'Retry', onAction }`, imported through `../notifications` (`NotificationAction` / `NotificationRequest`). Its `onAction` discards the store action's promise (`void actions.retryLanes(podId)`, `void actions.loadMoreEvents(podId)`, `void actions.retryRoutingMode()`) and catches nothing, because store actions resolve and never reject (`renderer-state.ts:23-28` at e2e3b0a). `WorkspaceAlerts.tsx` declares no notification or action type of its own. This encodes the binding frontend rule under 'Data fetching': 'A component states what data it needs; it does not orchestrate how the fetch happens'. The retry logic lives in the store, and the component only names which action to call.

C55. The header docblock of `WorkspaceAlerts.tsx` (`:1-20` at e2e3b0a) no longer says that E10 'is never dismissed, because there is no retry' (`:13-14`). It says that each of E8, E9 and E10 carries a Retry action and names the store action each one calls. It says that activating Retry removes the item at once and that a failed retry raises it again under the same key. It says that E10 is dismissed whenever `routingModeError` is `null`. It drops the citation `(session 20261111-0156-message-alerting)` (`:6`), stating the rows' keys and texts in place. The header docblock of `WorkspaceAlerts.test.tsx` (`:2-11`) mentions the Retry tests and drops its session citation (`:4-5`). Check: `git grep -c --untracked -E "20261[01][0-9]{2}-[0-9]{4}" -- src/renderer/src/shell/WorkspaceAlerts.tsx src/renderer/src/shell/WorkspaceAlerts.test.tsx` prints one line per file, each ending `:1`, at e2e3b0a, and at T3's tip prints nothing and exits 1.
C56. Every new test's name states its condition and its expected outcome, and claims no more than it asserts. This encodes the binding test discipline rules under `Naming`.

C57. No source file in the session states that a workspace load has no retry. `git grep -n -i "no retry" -- src/renderer` prints three lines at e2e3b0a (`renderer-state.ts:157`, `WorkspaceAlerts.tsx:14`, `store.ts:314`), and at T3's tip prints nothing and exits 1. Control, which must not change: `git grep -c -i "no retry" -- tests/unit/pod-manager/resume.test.ts` prints `tests/unit/pod-manager/resume.test.ts:2` both at e2e3b0a and at T3's tip.

C58. The repo-wide citation census, run at T3's tip after T1 and T2 have landed. (a) `git grep -l --untracked -E "20261[01][0-9]{2}-[0-9]{4}" -- src | wc -l` prints 12 at e2e3b0a and prints 8 at T3's tip. The four files that leave the list are `notifications/types.ts`, `contracts/renderer-state.ts`, `shell/WorkspaceAlerts.tsx` and `shell/WorkspaceAlerts.test.tsx`, and no file joins it. (b) `git grep -l --untracked .sir/sessions -- src | wc -l` prints 1 at e2e3b0a (`src/renderer/src/notifications/types.ts`) and prints 0 at T3's tip. The report lists the 8 surviving files.
